definitions.explanation: A person with the ability to judge the quality or authenticity of things — especially art, antiques, food, or other specialized items. Also refers to the ability itself.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{骨董品|こっとうひん}の{目利|めき}きだ。
examples.english: He is a connoisseur of antiques.

examples.japanese: {魚|さかな}の{目利|めき}きができる{人|ひと}は{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: Few people can judge the quality of fish.

examples.japanese: あの{店|みせ}の{店主|てんしゅ}は{目利|めき}きが{確|たし}かで、{良|い}いものばかり{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: The shop owner has a reliable eye for quality — only good items are on display.

notes:
USAGE:
Can refer either to the person ({目利|めき}き = connoisseur) or to the skill of judging ({目利|めき}きができる = to be able to appraise). Commonly used in contexts involving antiques, art, gemstones, fish, and other items where expert evaluation matters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目利|めき}きが{確|たし}か (having a reliable eye)
- {目利|めき}きができる (to be able to judge quality)
- {目利|めき}きの{力|ちから} (the ability to appraise)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鑑定|かんてい}: appraisal — more formal, often professional
- {通|つう}: connoisseur — broader term for someone knowledgeable
- {見|み}る{目|め}がある: to have a good eye — more casual expression
